brief: I'm Cass Whitfield, owner of Ironwood Tree Care in Asheville, North Carolina. We're certified arborists: pruning, removals, storm cleanup, and saving old trees people think are lost. Three crews, a bucket truck and a crane. The logo goes on the truck doors (cut vinyl, one color), our hard hats (a small one-color sticker), the website and its tab icon, and our shirts (embroidered on the chest). The name is "Ironwood Tree Care". No tagline. Not a generic green tree in a circle, please; every tree service has that. Don't ask me questions; make it.

I roast coffee in small batches in a 1940s feed mill in Davis, West Virginia, near Blackwater Falls. The company is Blackwater Roasting Co.; it's me (June Pak) and one roaster, a 15-kilo Diedrich. We sell bags online and to six cafes. The logo is stamped in one ink on our kraft-paper bags, embroidered on aprons, printed on cup sleeves, and used as the Instagram avatar and website icon. Name: "Blackwater Roasting Co.". No tagline. No coffee bean and no steaming cup. Don't ask me questions; make it.

We're Kettle River Brewing in Sandstone, Minnesota: a 7-barrel brewery and taproom in the old bank building on Main Street, run by brothers Erik and Nils Lund. We make lagers and a few seasonal ales; our best seller is Quarry Lager (4.6%). The taproom is open Thursday to Sunday, families and dogs welcome, and we sell cans to bars and liquor stores in the county. We have a logo (logo.svg). I need the brand system as a one-page guide for our can designer, our bartenders and whoever posts for us. Don't ask me questions; make it.

I'm Dr. Ana Ruiz, and I own Northfield Family Dental in Northfield, Minnesota: cleanings, fillings, crowns and kids' dentistry, with two dentists and four hygienists. A lot of our new patients are nervous adults who haven't been to a dentist in years, and parents bringing toddlers for a first visit. We take most insurance and have Saturday hours. We have a logo (logo.svg). I need the brand system as a one-page guide for our front desk, our website person and our mailers. Don't ask me questions; make it.

Parents in the Lakeview School District (Battle Creek, Michigan) use our app to see where their child's school bus is. The main screen shows one child's bus: Maya, bus 14, morning route, stop at Oak St. and Ridgeway Ave. Right now the bus is 3 stops away, about 6 minutes, and the driver is Mr. Dorsey. A map isn't needed; a simple route line with stops is enough. Screen 1 (screen.html): the bus 3 stops away. Screen 2 (offline.html): the same screen when the parent's phone has lost its connection; the last update was 2 minutes ago. Don't ask me questions; make it.

At the Clinton County 4-H Fair (Wilmington, Ohio), volunteers check in livestock with this app on their phones in the barn. The check-in screen for one exhibitor shows: exhibitor Hannah Brewer, age 14, Wilmington Clovers club; her animals: market hog "Tank" (ear tag 4471), market hog "Biscuit" (ear tag 4472), and a breeding gilt (ear tag 4490); weigh-in Monday 8 a.m. at the swine barn. The volunteer checks each animal in after seeing its tag and health papers. Screen 1 (screen.html): Hannah's check-in, with Tank already checked in and the other two not yet. Screen 2 (empty.html): the screen when the volunteer searches for an exhibitor number that has no animals entered. Don't ask me questions; make it.
